Forensics: re-attributed the 10/205 fold one pass UPSTREAM to the jump.c:754-860 normalisation (blocking it alone is sufficient), enumerated its eleven C-visible preconditions with file:line predicate

Rederive s8: fresh m2c blocked (missing jtbl, out-of-scope fix); MEM-source mechanism probe proves predicate B4 can never be target's real blocker (class kill) and reproduces target's exact v0/a0 regi

frontier.hypothesis: The true blocker for target's real (literal-0) selection_sound escape from jump.c's folds is a B8/B9-class predicate about the SHARED CALL TAIL at .L80074A20 (entered by both the row-toggle path's fallthrough and selection_sound's explicit j), not about the else-arm's value (B4 is now class-killed).
frontier.mechanism: jump.c:794-812/831 (LABEL_NUSES walk defeated by a CALL_INSN or a second FORWARD entry) or jump.c:832 (no_labels_between_p between the last conditional jump and the then-arm's terminating jump) - both predicates concern the LABEL the fallthrough/else path reaches, and target's real fallthrough here is not an isolated two-way if/else, it eventually merges into a tail (.L80074A20) reached from more than one caller.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the s7 xjdbg instrumented-cc1 trace (BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG=1) on the CURRENT (un-relocated, non-duplicated-call) floor-6 chassis - not the s7 relocated/duplicated variants - to see whether jump.c or a later cross-jump pass is what actually produces target's shared .L80074A20 tail, and whether LABEL_NUSES on that tail (not on the internal if/else label) is the real predicate in play. This has not been tried: s7's xjdbg trace only covered the relocated duplicated-call variant.

frontier.hypothesis: Hunk 9's jtbl_80015A0C table-offset residual (operand-only, lw v0,0(at) vs lw v0,24(at)) closes once the hand-transcribed array is deleted from src/text1a_b_mid_rodata.c in the same change that lands func_800747D8's real switch as committed C.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 emits a switch's ADDR_VEC into the .rodata of the TU containing the switch; the sandbox's isolated single-function build sees a placement/offset conflict against the hand array still present in text1a_b_mid_rodata.c rather than target's real layout.
frontier.next_probe: At final-submission assembly time only (not a src/text1b.c-only session): delete the jtbl_80015A0C array from src/text1a_b_mid_rodata.c in the same commit as func_800747D8's C body, then re-measure with sandbox --disable all --diff.

frontier.hypothesis: B9 (jump.c:832, a CODE_LABEL between the last conditional jump and the then-arm's terminating jump) is unreachable via a compound condition on this function's real single-byte field64 test (adjacent-field ORIF coalesces to one halfword compare, s7 finding) but may still be reachable via the shared-tail structure itself rather than the condition.
frontier.mechanism: Same jump.c:754-860 normalisation as B8; if the shared .L80074A20 tail is what supplies the extra CODE_LABEL or extra use, B9 and B8 may turn out to be the SAME underlying blocker described two different ways.
frontier.next_probe: Compare the xjdbg trace's label-use counts for .L80074A20 against LABEL_NUSES expectations from jump.c:787 to determine whether B8 and B9 collapse to one predicate for this function.
